objective_summary: Determine whether the Valdena Gelato Shop (northern Italy) has sufficient daily sales data, product-code mappings, weather data and holiday/events data to model the effect of hot days and public holidays on ice-cream sales by product, so the owner can plan orders a week ahead.

need_plans.interpretation: Daily sales data for ice-cream products sold at the Valdena Gelato Shop, aggregate-level (by product and date, not by customer), covering 2023-06-01 to 2026-03-31. Each row is one product sold on one day with a quantity or revenue. No customer-level data needed.
acceptance_criteria: Grain is daily-by-product (not weekly/monthly, not aggregated across products)
Covers the full history window 2023-06-01 to 2025-05-31
Covers the recent window 2025-06-01 to 2026-03-31
Contains a product identifier that can be joined to the product code mapping (N2)
Contains date and either quantity or revenue sold per product
likely_pitfalls: Sales data may only be total daily revenue with no product breakdown
Product codes may have changed in 2024 and old codes may be missing
Data may only exist for summer months (shop seasonal closure?)
Data may be stored in a POS system not yet exported
Grain could be weekly/monthly rather than daily

need_plans.interpretation: A static mapping table that translates product codes used before the 2024 code change to the current product codes, so that N1's sales can be tracked consistently across the full history window.
acceptance_criteria: Contains both old product codes (pre-2024) and new product codes (post-2024) as a pairwise mapping
Covers all products that appear in N1 sales data
If a product was discontinued, it is marked as such
If a product was introduced after the change, that is clear
likely_pitfalls: No mapping exists — codes were simply replaced without a crosswalk
Mapping is incomplete — some products dropped, some added
Mapping may exist only in human memory or in a spreadsheet not in the catalog
The code change might also include a rename or recipe change that makes products non-comparable

need_plans.interpretation: Daily maximum temperature in the city where the gelato shop is located (northern Italy, exact city to be selected by Scout), for every day from 2023-06-01 to 2026-03-31. Must come from a reliable weather reanalysis or station record.
external_data_hints: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (reanalysis) provides daily temperature maxima globally for any lat/lon, free and open — register entry api.open_meteo_archive
The Scout must choose a plausible northern Italian city (e.g. Verona, Milan, Turin, Bolzano) and set its coordinates; document the assumption.
acceptance_criteria: Covers every day from 2023-06-01 to 2026-03-31
Available at daily grain (daily maximum temperature, not hourly)
Geographic coordinates correspond to a plausible northern Italian city for the shop
Uses the registered Open-Meteo Historical Weather API
likely_pitfalls: Wrong coordinates (e.g. southern Italy) would give unrepresentative temperatures
API may not have real-time data yet for very recent days (latency of a few days)
Daily maximum may need to be computed from hourly data if not available as a daily variable
Free tier may have query limits — keep probe ranges small

need_plans.interpretation: A list of all Italian public holidays (national and possibly regional) for the years 2023 through 2026, one row per holiday date, so they can be flagged as binary features in the sales model.
external_data_hints: Nager.Date API (api.nager_public_holidays) provides public holidays by country and year, free and open — the register entry exists for UC2
If Nager.Date does not cover Italy's regional/local holidays, a secondary source (e.g. Italian open-data portal) may be needed
acceptance_criteria: Grain is daily: one row per holiday date
Includes national holidays of Italy
If regional holidays exist for the chosen region, they are included too (nice-to-have)
likely_pitfalls: Nager.Date may only cover national, not regional/local holidays
Some holidays fall on weekends and may or may not be observed on a weekday
API rate limits if polling multiple years

need_plans.interpretation: A daily calendar showing whether the shop was open/closed and any local events (festivals, markets) that could affect foot traffic, for 2023-06-01 to 2026-03-31.
external_data_hints: This is largely internal data (shop's own opening schedule, known closures for holidays, maintenance, etc.)
Local events could potentially be sourced from the municipality's tourism portal or open-data event calendar for the chosen city — but these may be incomplete or unstructured
acceptance_criteria: For each day in the windows, records whether the shop was open (yes/no)
Reasons for opening-day anomalies (closures, reduced hours, special events) are noted
Local events that could affect foot traffic are listed with dates
likely_pitfalls: No formal calendar may exist — the owner may say 'we're open every day in summer except Christmas'
Local events data may be unstructured, incomplete, or not available in a machine-readable format
Events that affect foot traffic can be positive (festivals, fairs) or negative (road works, bad weather)
The shop's opening hours may have changed seasonally or over the years

open_questions: What is the exact city/municipality where the Valdena Gelato Shop is located? This is needed to set coordinates for weather data and to look up regional holidays and local events.
Does the shop have a written (digital) record of its opening days and closures, or is that only in the owner's memory?
Does the product code change in 2024 affect all products or only some? Was a crosswalk table created at the time?
Is the shop open year-round or only seasonally (e.g. April–October)? This affects whether winter days with zero sales are meaningful.
Are sales recorded as quantities (number of scoops/cups) or as revenue (EUR), or both?
